candidate.blueprint_locator: Psychosocial Integrity, printed p.10 / PDF p.14: promote a therapeutic environment; incorporate behavioral management techniques; recognize nonverbal cues to physical and/or psychological stressors
candidate.blueprint_topic: Psychosocial Integrity — behavioral management / anger regulation
candidate.educational_objective: Teach clients to recognize early anger warning signs and use a brief timeout or relaxation technique before responding impulsively.

options.A: Notice early warning signs and use a timeout or slow deep breathing before reacting
options.B: Suppress all awareness of anger until the feeling disappears on its own
options.C: Confront the other person immediately before using any calming strategy
options.D: Ignore physical and emotional warning signs so they do not reinforce the anger

candidate.rationale: The U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs anger-control plan emphasizes identifying physical, behavioral, emotional, and cognitive warning signs and using behavioral tools such as timeout, deep breathing, and muscle relaxation. Therefore A is appropriate. B and D discourage awareness and constructive regulation, while C promotes immediate reaction rather than using a calming strategy first.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Anger-management planning includes recognizing warning signs and using behavioral regulation tools such as timeout, deep breathing, and muscle relaxation.
candidate.source_locator: Sections 'Your Anger Warning Signs' and 'Your Tools': physical/behavioral/emotional/cognitive warning signs; behavioral tools include Timeout, Deep Breathing, and Muscle Relaxation
